1.sa: उत्तरामखतया बलमाने सायमर्यमरथेऽभिसुमेरु । तन्मुखोल्लसितसारथिभासा पाटला स्फुरति पाशभृदाशा ॥ १ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the evening was approaching the chariot of the sun which was slightly tilted northwards was moving towards the mountain, driven by the charioteer Aruna. The tawnish radiance of Aruna, the elder brother of Garuda had created a distinctive splendour in the west by spreading all over. As a result of this, the west looked splendidly unique.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: उत्तरामखतया बलमाने सायम् अर्यमरथे अभिसुमेरु तत्-मुख-उल्लसित-सारथि-भासा पाटला स्फुरति पाशभृत्-आशा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सायम् उत्तरामखतया अभिसुमेरु बलमाने अर्यमरथे (सति) तत्-मुख-उल्लसित-सारथि-भासा पाटला पाशभृद्-आशा स्फुरति।
commentaries.gemini_summary: In the evening, as the sun's chariot moved toward Mount Meru facing northward, the western quarter (the direction of Varuna) shone in a glowing reddish-pink hue from the radiant light of the charioteer Aruna.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The saints Valakhilyas are the sons of the saint Krathu and Kriyadevi born in Swayambhuva Manvanthara. Those saints, sixty thousand in number always move with the sun's chariot. They offer Arghya to the sun with water and gems, singing the ruks of Samaveda every evening. The mellifluence of their music liquefies the gems in their hands along with those gems in the sea into a reddish liquid. The poet has exaggeratedly described that when this liquid is sprinkled on the sun and the chariot through offer of Arghya, in the evening, the sun appears red.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सायम् अन्तिक-चरत्-मुनि-पाली-गीत-साम-निनदेन शताङ्गे विद्रुत-अरुण-मणी-जल-सेकात् लोहितायति सरोरुह-बन्धुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सायम् अन्तिक-चरत्-मुनि-पाली-गीत-साम-निनदेन शताङ्गे विद्रुत-अरुण-मणी-जल-सेकात् सरोरुह-बन्धुः लोहितायति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: In the evening, the sun turns red as though sprayed with the liquid of rubies melted on his chariot by the melodious chanting of Sāmaveda hymns by the accompanying sages.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sun who always stays under the protection of Vishnupada (the sky) drove away all the darkness while he was rising. When the redness manifested in the sky, the sun shone splendidly and obtained his own visage of redness in the evening.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: निर्धुताखिलतमाः निजजन्म आरभ्य विष्णुपदसेवनशीलः स्वस्वरूपम् अगमत् परम् आविर्भूतम् एषः मिहिरः अरुणभावम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: निर्धुताखिलतमाः निजजन्म आरभ्य विष्णुपदसेवनशीलः एषः मिहिरः परम् आविर्भूतम् स्वस्वरूपम् अरुणभावम् अगमत्
commentaries.gemini_summary: Right from the moment of his rising, the sun dispelled all darkness and remained in the sky (the realm/feet of Vishnu), ultimately attaining his fully manifested true nature in a brilliant reddish glow.

4.sa: रागिणं स्वमवलोक्य निकामं रागिणां च विषमां गतिमीक्ष्य । वस्तुमापदपरागसमीपं मन्दमन्दमरविन्दकुटुम्बी ॥ ४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sun who nourishes the lotus was passionately attached to it. When he witnessed the agony experienced by sensualists, he apprehended that he too may have to experience that agony. Therefore, he decided to lead his life in the company of a man of renunciation and started moving towards the western mountain.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: रागिणम् स्वम् अवलोक्य निकामम् रागिणाम् च विषमाम् गतिम् ईक्ष्य वस्तुम् आपत् अपराग-समीपम् मन्द-मन्दम् अरविन्द-कुटुम्बी
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अरविन्द-कुटुम्बी स्वम् निकामम् रागिणम् अवलोक्य रागिणाम् विषमाम् गतिम् च ईक्ष्य वस्तुम् मन्द-मन्दम् अपराग-समीपम् आपत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Seeing himself full of red glow (passion) and mindful of the miserable plight suffered by passionate beings, the Sun (the kinsman of lotuses) slowly moved towards the western mountain (the vicinity of the dispassionate) to dwell there.

5.sa: विप्लवं व्रजति कान्तिकलत्रे पद्मिनीमपरवारिधिजाताम् । उद्विविक्षुहृदयो हरिदश्वो याचितुं तमगमत्तटिनीशम् ॥ ५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When Kanthi, the sun's consort died, he decided to marry Padmini (the lotus garden) born in the western ocean. Therefore he went to her father, the western ocean to seek his daughter from him.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: विप्लवम् व्रजति कान्ति-कलत्रे पद्मिनीम् अपर-वारिधि-जाताम् उद्विविक्षु-हृदयः हरिदश्वः याचितुम् तम् अगमत् तटिनीशम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: कान्तिकलत्रे विप्लवं व्रजति सति अपरवारिधिजातां पद्मिनीम् उद्विविक्षुहृदयः हरिदश्वः तं तटिनीशं याचितुम् अगमत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When his consort Kanti perished, the Sun (Haridashva), desiring to wed Padmini born of the western ocean, went to that ocean (the lord of rivers) to ask for her hand in marriage.

6.sa: सान्ध्यरागमयपावकदीप्तं लोकमीक्ष्य शकुनाभयमूढाः । प्राद्रवन् झडिति शावकवर्गं वीक्षितुं विहितभूरिनिनादाः ॥ ६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the birds saw the redness of the evening, they thought that the earth was burning. Apprehending that the fire may engulf their nests too, they flew very fast towards their nests, chirping very loudly to confirm their younger ones were safe.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सान्ध्यरागमयपावकदीप्तम् लोकम् ईक्ष्य शकुनाः भयमूढाः प्राद्रवन् झडिति शावकवर्गम् वीक्षितुम् विहितभूरिनिनादाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सान्ध्यरागमयपावकदीप्तम् लोकम् ईक्ष्य भयमूढाः विहितभूरिनिनादाः शकुनाः शावकवर्गम् वीक्षितुम् झडिति प्राद्रवन् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Seeing the world illuminated by the fiery red glow of twilight, the birds became bewildered by fear and, chirping loudly, rushed swiftly to their nests to check on their fledglings.

7.sa: पद्मिनी परिचिता सततं नः साबतात्मपतिना वियुतेति । सद्य एव वियुतानि बभूवुश्चक्रवाकपततां मिथुनानि ॥ ७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Bewailing that their acquaintance Kamalini (the group of lotus) was disunited from her consort, the sun, the ruddy geese separated from each other, the very next moment.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पद्मिनी परिचिता सततम् नः सा बत आत्मपतिना वियुता इति सद्यः एव वियुतानि बभूवुः चक्रवाकपतताम् मिथुनानि
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: नः सततं परिचिता सा पद्मिनी बत आत्मपतिना वियुता इति चक्रवाकपततां मिथुनानि सद्यः एव वियुतानि बभूवुः ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Grieving that the lotus pond—their constant acquaintance—was now separated from her consort (the sun), the pairs of ruddy geese also separated from each other at that very moment.

8.sa: एकचक्रमवलम्ब्य शताङ्गं बाधते विरहिणो मिहिरोसौ । इत्यवेत्य मदनः स्वयमाधादेकचक्रमयमाशु शताङ्गम् ॥ ८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thinking that the sun, riding the chariot which had only one wheel, afflicts, those men and women who are separated from their sweethearts, Manmatha immediately transformed the only ruddy goose (the wheel of the sun's chariot) into one having hundreds of limbs.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: एकचक्रम् अवलम्ब्य शताङ्गम् बाधते विरहिणः मिहिरः असौ इति अवेत्य मदनः स्वयम् आधात् एकचक्रम् अयम् आशु शताङ्गम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: असौ मिहिरः एकचक्रम् शताङ्गम् अवलम्ब्य विरहिणः बाधते इति अवेत्य मदनः स्वयम् अयम् एकचक्रम् आशु शताङ्गम् आधात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Observing that the sun torments separated lovers by mounting a one-wheeled chariot, Cupid personally and swiftly transformed the single ruddy goose (or wheel) into one possessing hundreds of limbs.

9.sa: अम्बराभिधहरिन्मणिपात्रे शङ्खविष्णुपदवारि दधानम् । हेमभाजनयुगं शशिभान्वोर्मण्डलद्वयमिदं कलयामः ॥ ९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the sun sets in the west and the moon rises in the east on a full moon evening, the sun-disc and the moon-disc appear like two golden cups containing the holy theertha. The sky looks like a plate made of sapphire. Thus when one beholds the Moon disc and the Sun-disc he feels as though they are two golden cups containing Shankhatheertha and Sri Vishnupadodaka placed in a plate made of Sapphire (Sky).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अम्बराभिध-हरिन्मणि-पात्रे शङ्ख-विष्णुपद-वारि दधानम् हेम-भाजन-युगम् शशि-भान्वोः मण्डल-द्वयम् इदम् कलयामः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अम्बराभिध-हरिन्मणि-पात्रे शङ्ख-विष्णुपद-वारि दधानम् शशि-भान्वोः इदम् मण्डल-द्वयं हेम-भाजन-युगं कलयामः।
commentaries.gemini_summary: We envision the rising moon and setting sun in the sapphire-like sky as two golden vessels holding holy conch water and the sacred water of Vishnu's feet.

10.sa: पूर्वभूमिधरगाधिसुतेन प्रेरितं रविमयाब्जभवास्त्रम् । तद्ग्रसत्यपरशैलवशिष्टं कोपवह्निरिव सान्ध्यमरीचिः ॥ १० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sages Vasista and Vishvamitra had a tiff in the past over the possession of Kamadhenu. Vasista then had made the Brahmastra shot by Vishvamitra ineffectual with his danda (pole) which had resulted in the fire of the latter's fury. Thus runs a story in purana. The poet keeping this in mind has said that Udayaparvatha (Vishvamithra) shot Brahmastra (the sun) at Astamayaparvatha (Vasista). When the latter swallowed it, the reddish sun rays in the evening looked splendid like the fire of Vishwamitra's fury.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्वभूमिधर-गाधिसुतेन प्रेरितम् रविमय-अब्जभव-अस्त्रम् तत् ग्रसति अपरशैल-वसिष्ठे कोप-वह्निः इव सान्ध्य-मरीचिः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पूर्वभूमिधर-गाधिसुतेन प्रेरितं तत् रविमय-अब्जभव-अस्त्रम् अपरशैल-वसिष्ठे ग्रसति सान्ध्य-मरीचिः कोप-वह्निः इव (अभात्)
commentaries.gemini_summary: Comparing the mountains to the sages Vishvamitra and Vashistha, as the western mountain (Vashistha) swallowed the sun-missile (Brahmastra) shot by the eastern mountain (Vishvamitra), the crimson evening glow shone like the fire of Vishvamitra's fury.

11.sa: अम्बुजेष्वरयुतेषु वियोक्तुं सायशाणकषणेन सुतीक्ष्णम् । किं चकार निजकञ्जकलम्बं तादृगेव यदभून्मुकुलं तत् ॥ ११ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The lotus is an arrow of flower of Manmatha. The petals of its bud looked like short legs. Then it appeared that Manmatha, with the purpose of shooting it on those who were bereft of their lovers, had sharpened his arrow of lotus by rubbing it against the grinding wheel of evening. Then the lotus bud looked like a sharpened arrow.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अम्बुजेषुः अरयुतेषु वियोक्तुम् साय-शाण-कषणेन सुतीक्ष्णम् किम् चकार निज-कञ्ज-कलम्बम् तादृक् एव यत् अभूत् मुकुलम् तत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अम्बुजेषुः अरयुतेषु वियोक्तुम् साय-शाण-कषणेन निज-कञ्ज-कलम्बम् सुतीक्ष्णम् किम् चकार, यत् तत् मुकुलम् तादृक् एव अभूत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As evening fell, the closing lotus bud appeared so pointed that the poet wonders whether Kāmadeva had sharpened his lotus-arrow on the whetstone of twilight to shoot at those separated from their beloveds.

12.sa: वीक्ष्य पद्मविपिनेषु पुरा यत्केसरिश्रियमदुद्रवदारात् । तां विलोक्य शिथिलां पुनरागात्तत्तथैव तिमिरद्विपवृन्दम् ॥ १२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The darkness fled the place when it saw the saffronish radiance in lotus gardens (the moment the sun rose) just like the herd of elephants runs away at the sight of lions. But when the sun set and the lotus buds lost their radiance, the darkness once again spread everywhere just like those elephants return when the lion becomes old and fragile.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वीक्ष्य पद्मविपिनेषु पुरा यत् केसरिश्रियम् अदुद्रवत् आरात् ताम् विलोक्य शिथिलाम् पुनः आगात् तत् तथा एव तिमिरद्विपवृन्दम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पुरा पद्मविपिनेषु केसरिश्रियम् वीक्ष्य यत् आरात् अदुद्रवत् तत् तिमिरद्विपवृन्दम् ताम् शिथिलाम् विलोक्य तथा एव पुनः आगात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The herd of elephants in the form of darkness, which had earlier fled far away upon seeing the lion-like splendor of the lotus filaments at sunrise, returned as soon as it saw that splendor fade at sunset.

13.sa: अर्चयन्मधुकरच्छलशालिग्राममेष समयाभिधयोगी । सायमम्बुजसमुद्गममध्ये सन्निधाय विदधेऽस्य च मुद्राम् ॥ १३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The saint Kalapurusha kept the Saligramas (the bees) in caskets (the lotus) after worshipping them and locked those caskets in the evening. Explanation: The poet has dexterously described that those who saw the bees hovering around the lotus getting trapped in them when those flowers closed their petals in the evening felt as though the saint Kalapurusha was keeping those bees in the lotus and locking them as a saint worships Saligramas and locks those Saligramas in caskets.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अर्चयन् मधुकर-छल-शालिग्रामम् एषः समय-अभिध-योगी सायम् अम्बुज-समुद्ग-मध्ये सन्निधाय विदधे अस्य च मुद्राम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: एषः समयाभिधयोगी मधुकरच्छलशालिग्रामम् अर्चयन् सायं अम्बुजसमुद्गमध्ये सन्निधाय अस्य च मुद्राम् विदधे ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Personifying Time (Samaya) as an ascetic yogi, the verse describes how in the evening he worshipped the black bees—metaphorically seen as Shaligrama stones—placed them inside the lotus-caskets, and sealed them shut by closing the petals.

14.sa: पद्मिनी पतिशुचा अमरालीकङ्कणे निरसितुं कृतचेतः । अब्जपाणिमनिलेन विलोलं हन्त हन्त समकोचयदाशु ॥ १४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Padmini (the lotus) who could not bear with the agony of separation from her consort, the sun, in the evening shrivelled her hand (the lotus swinging to and fro due to the force of the wind) in her effort to remove the bangles (the rows of bees). Explanation: Just as a woman shrivels her hand while removing bangles, the lotus shrivelled her hand in the evening. This is how the poet has described the act of lotus shriveling into a bud when the sun sets.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पद्मिनी पतिशुचा अमरालीकङ्कणे निरसितुम् कृतचेतः अब्जपाणिम् अनिलेन विलोलम् हन्त हन्त समकोचयत् आशु
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पतिशुचा पद्मिनी अमरालीकङ्कणे निरसितुम् कृतचेतः अनिलेन विलोलम् अब्जपाणिम् आशु समकोचयत् हन्त हन्त
commentaries.gemini_summary: Stricken with grief over separation from her husband (the sun), the lotus plant (personified as a grieving wife) swiftly contracted her lotus-hand, trembling in the wind, in order to cast off her bangles (the rows of bees).

15.sa: रश्मिजालमधिकं भुवनाब्धेः कालधीवरवरः परिकृष्य । पङ्कशैवललुठज्झषसंघं ध्वान्ततारनिभतो गगनेऽधात् ॥ १५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The fisherman Kalapurusha desired to catch fish in the ocean (the world). It appeared as though he caught the fish which were feeling disturbed in the slush using the sun rays as net and kept them in the sky. It is the feeling of the poet that those shining stars in the sky are the fish caught by the fisherman, Kalapurusha.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: रश्मिजालम् अधिकम् भुवनाब्धेः कालधीवरवरः परिकृष्य पङ्कशैवललुठज्झषसंघम् ध्वान्ततारनिभतः गगने अधात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: कालधीवरवरः भुवनाब्धेः अधिकम् रश्मिजालम् परिकृष्य पङ्कशैवललुठज्झषसंघम् ध्वान्ततारनिभतः गगने अधात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Metaphorically depicting nightfall, the expert fisherman of Time (Kāla) is envisioned as pulling up his vast net of sunbeams from the ocean of the world and depositing the thrashing fish along with moss and mud into the sky, where they appear in the guise of darkness and stars.

16.sa: चन्द्रदीधितिनटीं दिवसान्तः सादरं नटयितुं भुवनान्तः । संविकीर्य किमु तारसुमौघं ध्वान्तनीलयवनीं पुरतोऽधात् ॥ १६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Before a danseuse commences her programme, the organiser prays to the devatha and performs pooja to the stage by spreading flowers in front of it. Then the stage remains covered with a black screen. Afterwards the danseuse enters the stage by moving the screen aside. Then they move the screen upwards. Keeping this in mind, the poet has described that when it became dark in the evening, it looked like that black screen. It appeared as if white jasmine and other flowers were showered on the stage when stars became visible in the sky. Finally, when the moon rose, the moonlight (the danseuse) started dancing on the stage.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चन्द्रदीधितिनटीम् दिवसान्तः सादरम् नटयितुम् भुवनान्तः संविकीर्य किमु तारसुमौघम् ध्वान्तनीलयवनीम् पुरतः अधात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दिवसान्तः भुवनान्तः चन्द्रदीधितिनटीम् सादरम् नटयितुम् तारसुमौघम् संविकीर्य पुरतः ध्वान्तनीलयवनीम् अधात् किमु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet imagines nightfall as a stage manager who, wishing respectfully to make the moonlight-danseuse perform on the cosmic stage, scatters a shower of star-flowers and hangs a dark blue curtain of darkness before the show.

17.sa: वर्षके सति तमिस्रजलौघं व्योमनामनि घनाघनसंधे । दीपिकास्तत इतो वलमानाः शक्रगोपनिकरा इव रेजुः ॥ १७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the sky (clouds) was showering darkness (heavy rains), when the flames of lamps lit in the houses were wavering due to the force of the blowing wind and when the people were moving here and there holding those lamps in their hands, those lamps looked splendid like fire flies.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वर्षके सति तमिस्र-जल-ओघम् व्योम-नामनि घनाघन-संधे दीपिकाः ततः इतः वलमानाः शक्रगोप-निकराः इव रेजुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: व्योम-नामनि घनाघन-संधे तमिस्र-जल-ओघम् वर्षके सति ततः इतः वलमानाः दीपिकाः शक्रगोप-निकराः इव रेजुः ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the dense gathering of rain clouds across the sky poured down floods of darkness, lamps moving and flickering hither and thither shone brilliantly like swarms of glowing fireflies.

18.sa: दग्धतामुपगतेषु मनोभूर्वह्निनायुगपदेषु निकामम् । भज्जिते सति हि शार्वरधूमे रेजुरग्निकणिका इव दीपाः ॥ १८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The fire (Manmatha) incinerated the houses of those who were bereft of their sweethearts. The smoke (darkness) disappeared. Then those burning lamps looked beautiful like sparks of fire.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: दग्धताम् उपगतेषु मनोभूः वह्निना अयुगपदेषु निकामम् भज्जिते सति हि शार्वर-धूमे रेजुः अग्नि-कणिकाः इव दीपाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मनोभूः वह्निना अयुगपदेषु निकामम् दग्धताम् उपगतेषु शार्वर-धूमे भज्जिते सति हि दीपाः अग्निकणिकाः इव रेजुः ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the dwellings of the separated lovers were intensely burnt by the fire of Cupid and the smoke-like nocturnal darkness was dispersed, the lamps shone brightly like glowing sparks of fire.

19.sa: भानुकार्तयुगधर्मविलोपाज्जृम्भिते जगति शार्वरपापे । अस्फुरंस्तत इतः किल दीपा रक्षिता इव तपोङ्कुररेखाः ॥ १९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: All the four feet of Dharma would be in perfect condition in Krithayuga, whereas Dharma would be having three feet in Trethayuga, two feet in Dwaparayuga and only one foot in Kaliyuga. That single foot too would disappear as a result of the ill influence of sin and only a fraction of Dharma would exist in Kaliyuga. When the sun who is the Dharma of Krithayuga disappeared, the sin of darkness triumphed like it did in Kaliyuga. Those lamps lit here and there sparkled like the rows of sprouts of Varnashrama Dharma protected and preserved for Krithayuga.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: भानु-कार्तयुग-धर्म-विलोपात् जृम्भिते जगति शार्वर-पापे अस्फुरन् ततः इतः किल दीपाः रक्षिताः इव तपः-अङ्कुर-रेखाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: भानु-कार्तयुग-धर्म-विलोपात् जगति शार्वर-पापे जृम्भिते (सति) ततः इतः रक्षिताः तपः-अङ्कुर-रेखाः इव दीपाः अस्फुरन् किल ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon the disappearance of the sun—just like the loss of Krita Yuga's complete righteousness—nocturnal darkness (akin to sin) expanded over the world, while scattered lamps flickered brightly like carefully protected sprouts of dharma.

20.sa: कालनामनिजनाटकमध्ये दीपिकावलिनिभेन विधात्रा । उद्यदिन्दुमयदीपवरस्य प्रागतानि किमु सूचनभङ्गी ॥ २० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: It appeared as if Brahma was indicating the arrival of the bright moon light by getting those lamps lit during the intermission of his play "Kalapurusha charitha". Explanation: The Sootradhara (stage manager) gives prior information about the role before the actor in that role appears on the stage. Likewise, people look at the moon after lighting the lamps in the evening daily.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: काल-नाम-निज-नाटक-मध्ये दीपिका-आवलि-निभेन विधात्रा उद्यत्-इन्दु-मय-दीप-वरस्य प्राक् अतानि किमु सूचन-भङ्गी
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: विधात्रा काल-नाम-निज-नाटक-मध्ये दीपिका-आवलि-निभेन उद्यत्-इन्दु-मय-दीप-वरस्य सूचन-भङ्गी प्राक् अतानि किमु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: It appeared as if the Creator, in the midst of His drama named Time, presented an advance indication of the grand lamp of the rising moon under the guise of lighting rows of evening lamps.

21.sa: चन्द्रिकापि यदि संघटिताशा ध्वान्तदीपततिसंगतिकाले । किं त्रिवेणिकथयास्ति कवीनां स्वल्पतोपि जहतां पुनरुक्तिम् ॥ २१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the pitch darkness, the light emitted by the rows of lamps and the moon light meet each other, it becomes the confluence of the three. Hence where is the necessity of describing the confluence of the rivers Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswathi for the poets who avoid even the slightest degree of tautology. Explanation: The colours of the Ganges, the Yamuna and the Saraswathi are dazzling white, black and red respectively, and it is customary to term their confluence as "Triveni Sangama". Therefore it is the feeling of the poet that it becomes tautological to describe their confluence when he has already given description of the confluence of moon light, pitch darkness and the light from the rows of lamps representing dazzling white, black and red respectively.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चन्द्रिका अपि यदि संघटित-आशा ध्वान्त-दीप-तति-संगति-काले किम् त्रिवेणि-कथया अस्ति कवीनाम् स्वल्पतः अपि जहताम् पुनरुक्तिम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यदि ध्वान्त-दीप-तति-संगति-काले संघटित-आशा चन्द्रिका अपि (भवति), (तदा) स्वल्पतः अपि पुनरुक्तिं जहतां कवीनां त्रिवेणि-कथया किं (प्रयोजनम्) अस्ति?
commentaries.gemini_summary: When moonlight fills all quarters at the time darkness mingles with the light of lamp-rows, forming a confluence of white, dark, and red hues, poets who avoid even the slightest repetition have no need to speak of the Triveni confluence.

22.sa: व्योमगुग्गुलुतरोर्धवला निर्यासपङ्किरिव तारकराजिः । शार्वरेभकषणा लुलिताः किं तत्कणा भुवि तमोमणिदम्भात् ॥ २२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sky itself is a timber tree yielding olibanum. The rows of stars in the sky appeared like the path covered by the white essence of olibanum. When the darkness (elephant) rubbed its body against the sky (olibanum tree) patches of darkness which looked like chips of timber spread on the ground in the form of gems of darkness.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्योम-गुग्गुलु-तरोः धवला निर्यास-पङ्क्तिः इव तारक-राजिः शार्वर-इभ-कषणात् लुलिताः किं तत्-कणाः भुवि तमः-मणि-दम्भात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: धवला तारकराजिः व्योमगुग्गुलुतरोः निर्यासपङ्क्तिः इव (अस्ति) । शार्वरेभकषणात् लुलिताः तत्कणाः तमोमणिदम्भात् भुवि (पतिताः) किम् ?
commentaries.gemini_summary: The white row of stars resembles resin oozing from the sky imagined as a fragrant guggulu tree, while the dark patches on the earth, disguised as dark gems, seem to be its fragments shaken loose by the rubbing of the elephant of night.

23.sa: शर्वरीशशरदा परिसृष्टः शार्वरव्रजघनाघनसंधः । दृश्यते स्म शनकैर्धवलश्रीश्चन्द्रिकालहरिकामपदिश्य ॥ २३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The clouds look whitish during the autumn. The poet has described that the moon of the autumn pervading through those clouds (darkness) has made them to appear whitish like moon light.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शर्वरीशशरदा परिसृष्टः शार्वरव्रजघनाघनसंधः दृश्यते स्म शनकैः धवलश्रीः चन्द्रिकालहरिकाम् अपदिश्य
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: शर्वरीशशरदा परिसृष्टः शार्वरव्रजघनाघनसंधः चन्द्रिकालहरिकाम् अपदिश्य शनकैः धवलश्रीः दृश्यते स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Touched by the autumnal moon, the dense gathering of dark clouds gradually assumed a brilliant white radiance under the guise of rolling waves of moonlight.

24.sa: कालकालवदनेन तमिस्रैः श्मश्रुलेन शरदेन च तारैः । अम्बरेण वियुजां ग्रसनार्थं सान्ध्यरागरसना प्रसृता नु ॥ २४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The stars of the autumn look like the moustache of Akashapurusha (The sky). The evening appeared like the reddish tongue stretched out of the mouth of such Akashapurusha who had his face covered by darkness resembling that of Yama, the god of death, in order to swallow and destroy those who were separated from their sweethearts.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: काल-काल-वदनेन तमिस्रैः श्मश्रुलेन शरदेन च तारैः अम्बरेण वियुजाम् ग्रसन-अर्थम् सान्ध्य-राग-रसना प्रसृता नु
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तमिस्रैः काल-काल-वदनेन शरदेन तारैः च श्मश्रुलेन अम्बरेण वियुजां ग्रसन-अर्थं सान्ध्य-राग-रसना प्रसृता नु (इव भाति)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The autumnal sky, dark as the face of Yama and sporting a moustache of stars, seemed to stretch out the red twilight as its tongue to devour lovers pining in separation.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Those girls disunited from their sweethearts experience more grief during the night. The darkness during the night causes anguish of separation in them. The darkness gradually becomes more and more intense in the evening like the ocean does at the time of universal destruction, as though to cause their death. This sea of darkness pervades upto the starry region. The glow worms glow in groups then. Those glow worms were looking like the reflection of those stars which were hiding behind the curtain of darkness.

The darkness spread densely as the sun set in the evening. The blacksmith Manmatha intensely heated an iron ball in the fire of separation experienced by the lotus grown in sea. Then he blew air through the pair of bellows of sea tides to blaze up that fire of separation. The red iron ball heated intensely in that fire is now moving up the horizon as the hue of moon rise.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मार-कारु-कृत-आधतमिस्रम् गोलम् अब्धि-नलिनी-विरह-अग्नेः ऊर्मि-भस्त्र-पवनैः अति-तप्तम् शीत-रश्मि-उदय-राग-मिषेण
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मार-कारु-कृत-आधतमिस्रम् अब्धि-नलिनी-विरह-अग्नेः ऊर्मि-भस्त्र-पवनैः अति-तप्तम् गोलम् शीत-रश्मि-उदय-राग-मिषेण [व्यराजत]।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Under the guise of the reddish glow of the rising moon, an iron sphere appears to have been intensely heated in the fire of separation of the ocean-lotus fanned by the bellows-wind of the waves, forged amidst the dense darkness by the blacksmith Kāma.

27.sa: निर्यतो भुवि निलिम्पतटिन्याः कौमुदीमिषपयःप्रकरस्य । मौक्तिकभ्रम इव प्रवकाशे पूर्वशैलशिखरे शशिबिम्बम् ॥ २७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The water current of moon-light (Current of milk) started showering down on earth from Akashaganga. The moon disc rising above the eastern mountain scintillated like the swirl accompanied by torrent of pearls.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: निर्यतः भुवि निलिम्पतटिन्याः कौमुदी-मिष-पयः-प्रकरस्य मौक्तिक-भ्रमः इव प्रवकाशे पूर्व-शैल-शिखरे शशि-बिम्बम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: निलिम्पतटिन्याः भुवि निर्यतः कौमुदीमिषपयःप्रकरस्य मौक्तिकभ्रमः इव शशिबिम्बम् पूर्वशैलशिखरे प्रवकाशे ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the flood of water in the guise of moonlight descended to earth from the celestial river (Akashaganga), the moon's orb rising upon the eastern mountain peak shone brilliantly like a whirlpool of pearls.

28.sa: पूर्वसिन्धुसलिलेन निषेक्तुं तारकाङ्कुरततिं ततरश्मि । इन्दुबिम्बपिटकं किमु दने दक्षिणोत्तरहरित्परिणीभ्याम् ॥ २८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The moon disc appears like the basket of bamboo tied by the rope of rays spread in the directions of north and south and being swung by two devathas who are the rulers of north and south, in order to supply water to the sprouts of stars, from the eastern sea.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्वसिन्धुसलिलेन निषेक्तुम् तारकाङ्कुरततिम् ततरश्मि इन्दुबिम्बपिटकम् किमु दने दक्षिणोत्तरहरित्परिणीभ्याम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तारकाङ्कुरततिं पूर्वसिन्धुसलिलेन निषेक्तुं दक्षिणोत्तरहरित्परिणीभ्याम् ततरश्मि इन्दुबिम्बपिटकं दने किमु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The lunar disc, woven with spreading rays like a watering basket, appeared as though it were being held and swung by the deities of the northern and southern directions to irrigate the sprouting sprouts of stars with the waters of the eastern ocean.

29.sa: उक्षिपन्त्युदयरक्तिममौलिप्रावृतिं हरिदिशा हरिणाक्षी । मन्दमिन्दुवदनं किमुदञ्चत्याहृता नटितुमम्बररङ्गे ॥ २९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the moon rose, the redness of the moon rise disappeared. The poet has exaggeratedly described that the atmosphere then appeared as if the danseuse (the east) who came to dance on the stage (the sky) has moved aside the red curtain above her head to show her moon like face to the audience.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: उत्क्षिपन्ती उदय-रक्तिम-मौलि-प्रावृतिम् हरिद्-दिशा हरिण-अक्षी मन्दम् इन्दु-वदनम् किम् उदञ्चति आहृता नटितुम् अम्बर-रङ्गे
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अम्बर-रङ्गे नटितुम् आहृता हरिणाक्षी हरिद्-दिशा उदय-रक्तिम-मौलि-प्रावृतिम् उत्क्षिपन्ती मन्दम् इन्दु-वदनम् उदञ्चति किम् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet imagines the eastern quarter as a deer-eyed dancer who has stepped onto the stage of the sky, slowly unveiling her moon-like face as she pushes back the red morning-glow covering her head.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Those who perform yaga for a malevolent purpose use butter for homa. Now Manmatha decided to conduct Abhicharayaga to cause affliction as intense as the agony of death, to those men who were bereft of their sweethearts. The poet has exaggerated that the moon disc which was moving whimsically above the sea at the time of moon rise served as melted butter for Manmatha to conduct Abhicharayaga.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पान्थ-संहति-कृते कृत-चेताः यष्टुम् आदित हविः नवनीतम् द्रौतम् एषः विषमेषुः उदन्वत्-मौलि-गोल-विधु-बिम्ब-निभेन
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पान्थसंहतिकृते यष्टुम् कृतचेताः एषः विषमेषुः उदन्वन्मौलिगोलविधुबिम्बनिभेन द्रौतं नवनीतं हविः आदित ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Resolved to perform a malevolent rite to torment separated travelers, Cupid (Manmatha) gathered sacrificial oblation in the form of melted butter under the guise of the spherical moon rising over the crest of the ocean.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The blue sky is a big lake. The moon roaming in the sky is the swan. The swan separates the milk from water and drinks it. Likewise the rising moon separated the pair of ruddy geese from each other which were intimately close like milk and water. Alas! this is really regrettable.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चक्रवाक-मिथुन-च्छल-नीर-क्षीरयोः अकृत हन्त विभागम् व्योम-नाम-सरसी-कृत-केलिः सायम् एषः सित-रश्मि-मरालः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हन्त व्योम-नाम-सरसी-कृत-केलिः एषः सित-रश्मि-मरालः सायम् चक्रवाक-मिथुन-च्छल-नीर-क्षीरयोः विभागम् अकृत
commentaries.gemini_summary: Alas, sporting in the lake of the sky at evening, this swan of the white-rayed moon separated the pair of Chakravaka birds, who were intimately mingled like milk and water.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After sacrificing the animal during yaga, they would take out "vapa" (diaphragm) from its heart, rinse it in ghee, burn it in fire and take it before the sun on "Shrapani" a thorny device. Likewise when the sun set in the evening and redness of moon rise appeared in the sky, the evening (performer of yajna) poured the rays (ghee) on the soft moon-disc (diaphragm) and cooked it in the redness of moon rise (fire) in Poorvadri (the altar of Yajna). Then he kept it in the sky (thorny device).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्वभूमिधर-वेदि-गत-उद्यत्-राग-वह्नि-उपरि-रश्मि-घृत-आक्ताम् संपचन् विधु-वपाम् समयः अधात् योजित-अम्बर-वपा-श्रपणीकाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: समयः पूर्वभूमिधर-वेदि-गत-उद्यत्-राग-वह्नि-उपरि-रश्मि-घृत-आक्ताम् योजित-अम्बर-वपा-श्रपणीकाम् विधु-वपाम् संपचन् अधात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Metaphorically portraying the evening as a sacrificial priest, the verse describes Time cooking the lunar disc (the sacrificial omentum) in the rising crimson glow of dusk (the fire) upon the eastern mountain (the altar), anointing it with rays (ghee), and raising it upon the sky (the roasting spit).

33.sa: अन्धकारनिभकल्पविरामे विप्लुतं जगदिदं विधुवेधाः । किं ससर्ज तदिदं यदमुष्मिन्नुद्यते सति परं विललास ॥ ३३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The world appeared destroyed in dense darkness of the night just as it did during the era of extinction of all life. But when the moon rose, the world which appeared to have perished, once again looked splendid as if getting created again. The poet who saw the world which was invisible in the darkness, regaining its splendour in the moonlight, has exaggeratedly described that the moon as Brahma must have recreated this world which appeared destroyed in darkness.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अन्धकार-निभ-कल्प-विरामे विप्लुतम् जगत् इदम् विधु-वेधाः किम् ससर्ज तत् इदम् यत् अमुष्मिन् उद्यते सति परम् विललास
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अन्धकार-निभ-कल्प-विरामे विप्लुतम् इदम् जगत् विधु-वेधाः किम् ससर्ज ? यत् अमुष्मिन् उद्यते सति तत् इदम् परम् विललास ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Did the moon, as the creator Brahmā, fashion this world afresh after it was submerged in deluge-like darkness? For upon the moon's rising, the entire world shone forth brilliantly once more.

34.sa: संयमीन्द्रविविधोक्तिविलासं श्रोतुमुत्सुकमना दिवसान्ते । उन्ममज्ज जलधेर्विधुदम्भाद्दर्शयन् फणगणान् फणिराजः ॥ ३४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the moon was rising above the horizon in the evening, he was spreading reddish golden rays all over. Those who saw those rays felt as though Sesha who was yearning to listen to the distinctive style of delivery of discourse by Sri Raghavendra, was emerging above the sea, disguised as moon and stretching out his hoods in the form of rays.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: संयमीन्द्रविविधोक्तिविलासम् श्रोतुम् उत्सुकमनाः दिवसान्ते उन्ममज्ज जलधेः विधुदम्भात् दर्शयन् फणगणान् फणिराजः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दिवसान्ते संयमीन्द्रविविधोक्तिविलासम् श्रोतुम् उत्सुकमनाः फणिराजः फणगणान् दर्शयन् विधुदम्भात् जलधेः उन्ममज्ज ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: At the close of day, the king of serpents (Adishesha), deeply eager to listen to the graceful and varied discourses of Sri Raghavendra, seemed to rise from the ocean in the guise of the moon, displaying his multiple hoods in the form of spreading rays.

35.sa: रक्तयोरभिमुखं स्थिथिभाजोः पद्मिनीकुमुदिनीपरिणेन्नोः । कः करोतु बत बिम्बविवेकं नापरत्र यदि लक्ष्मविलासः ॥ ३५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Who would be able to differentiate between the sun disc and the moon disc, if the distinctive stain in the moon disc becomes invisible, when the sun, the sweetheart of Kamalini (Lotus) and the moon, the sweetheart of Kumudini (water lily) both reddish in colour, face each other at the time of sunset and moon-rise taking place simultaneously in west and east respectively?
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: रक्तयोः अभिमुखम् स्थितिभाजोः पद्मिनी-कुमुदिनी-परिणेत्रोः कः करोतु बत बिम्ब-विवेकम् न अपरत्र यदि लक्ष्म-विलासः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अभिमुखम् स्थितिभाजोः रक्तयोः पद्मिनीकुमुदिनीपरिणेत्रोः अपरत्र यदि लक्ष्मविलासः न (स्यात्, तर्हि) बत कः बिम्बविवेकम् करोतु?
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the sun and the moon—the respective consorts of the day-lotus and night-lily—stand facing each other, both appearing red, who could tell their discs apart if not for the distinctive mark (spot) visible upon the moon?

36.sa: पूर्वशैलवृषभाचलदृशयं देवतीर्थमधिगम्य सुधांशुम् । हृष्यतोस्य भुवनस्य न मोघं चन्द्रिकात्मसुकृतत्वमयासीत् ॥ ३६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Those who visit a holy place and worship the God gets punya. Similarly those people who had Devatheertha in the form of ambrosial rays of moon which looked like cataract of Vrishabhadri were elated. As a result of this, they secured punya in the form of moon light.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्वशैल-वृषभाचल-दृश्यम् देवतीर्थम् अधिगम्य सुधांशुम् हृष्यतः अस्य भुवनस्य न मोघम् चन्द्रिका-आत्म-सुकृतत्वम् अयासीत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पूर्वशैल-वृषभाचल-दृश्यम् सुधांशुम् देवतीर्थम् अधिगम्य हृष्यतः अस्य भुवनस्य चन्द्रिका-आत्म-सुकृतत्वम् मोघम् न अयासीत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon reaching the moon, which is like holy water (Devatirtha) seen rising on the eastern mountain (or Vrishabhachala), the delighted world's attainment of religious merit in the form of moonlight did not go in vain.

37.sa: विष्टपे विधुरुचा विद्धाने क्षीरसागरनिमज्जनकेलिम् । पाठकर्म स समाप्य सरस्यां मङ्गुमन्त उदयुङ्क्त यतीन्द्रः ॥ ३७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: While the whole world was rejoicing in the ocean of moon light, Sri Raghavendra, the great saint got up to take a plunge in the lake behind the Mutt after completing his daily routine of teaching and delivering discourse.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: विष्टपे विधु-रुचा विद्धाने क्षीर-सागर-निमज्जन-केलिम् पाठ-कर्म सः समाप्य सरस्याम् मङ्गुम् अन्तः उदयुङ्क्त यतीन्द्रः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: विधुरुचा विष्टपे क्षीरसागरनिमज्जनकेलिम् विद्धाने (सति) सः यतीन्द्रः पाठकर्म समाप्य सरस्याम् अन्तः मङ्गुम् उदयुङ्क्त ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the brilliant moonlight made the world look as if it were joyfully submerged in the ocean of milk, the supreme ascetic Raghavendra finished his daily teaching duties and prepared to take a deep plunge into the lake.

38.sa: स्नानकर्म विरचय्य वसानो वाससी त्रिपदया सवितारम् । वन्दते स्म तदनु त्रिदशेशं विष्णुमैहत समर्हितुमर्हम् ॥ ३८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After his bath, the great saint enclothed himself with two ochry reddish clothes and worshipped Savthiru namaka Lord Sri Narayana chanting Gayathri Manthra. Then after completing Pranava and Gayathri Japas, he started the pooja of that Lord of Lords Sri Moolaramachandra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: स्नानकर्म विरचय्य वसानः वाससी त्रिपदया सवितारम् वन्दते स्म तदनु त्रिदशेशम् विष्णुम् ऐहत समर्हितुम् अर्हम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: स्नानकर्म विरचय्य वाससी वसानः त्रिपदया सवितारम् वन्दते स्म तदनु अर्हम् त्रिदशेशम् विष्णुम् समर्हितुम् ऐहत
commentaries.gemini_summary: After completing his ritual bath and donning two garments, he worshipped the Sun-god using the three-footed Gayatri mantra; subsequently, he prepared to perform the worship of the most worthy Lord Vishnu, the master of the gods.

39.sa: अर्पयन्भगवते सुममाल्यं प्रीणयन् सपयसा च फलेन । हेमपात्रविलसद्धनसारारार्तिकेण कलयंस्तमहृष्यन् ॥ ३९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra decorated Lord Sri Moolarama with garlands of fresh flowers, offered oblation of milk and fruits to the Lord and also mangalarati in a golden plate. Thus the great saint forgot himself getting immersed in an emotionally delightful world after worshipping Lord Sri Moolarama in profound devotion.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अर्पयन् भगवते सुममाल्यम् प्रीणयन् सपयसा च फलेन हेमपात्रविलसद्-घनसार-आरार्तिकेण कलयन् तम् अहृष्यत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: भगवते सुममाल्यम् अर्पयन् सपयसा फलेन च प्रीणयन् हेमपात्रविलसद्-घनसार-आरार्तिकेण तम् कलयन् [सः] अहृष्यत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Offering a garland of flowers to the Lord, pleasing Him with milk and fruits, and performing the arati with camphor shining in a golden vessel, Sri Raghavendra rejoiced in supreme bliss.

40.sa: मन्त्रपुष्पमधिमौलि दधानो यन्त्रितान्यविषयो रघुनेतुः । सादरं दरनिमीलितनेत्रः स्तोतुमारभत संयमिधुर्यः ॥ ४० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the great saint put flowers consecrated with mantra on his head. Then forgetting this world, he sat with eyes closed and started extolling the Lord Sri Moolarama with profound devotion meditating on the Lord in his lotus heart.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मन्त्रपुष्पम् अधिमौलि दधानः यन्त्रित-अन्य-विषयः रघुनेतुः सादरम् दर-निमीलित-नेत्रः स्तोतुम् आरभत संयमि-धुर्यः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अधिमौलि मन्त्रपुष्पं दधानः यन्त्रितान्यविषयः दरनिमीलितनेत्रः संयमिधुर्यः रघुनेतुः सादरं स्तोतुम् आरभत।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Placing the consecrated flowers upon his head with all other worldly distractions restrained and his eyes gently closed, the foremost of ascetics (Raghavendra) devoutly began to extol Lord Rama.

41.sa: वेदसिद्धमणुतोप्यणुभावं मोददायि महतोपि महत्त्वम् । बिभ्रतं प्रथयितुं मनवे त्वां मीनतां शरणयामि भवन्तम् ॥ ४१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: We are in Vyvasvatha Manvantara now which is the seventh one. Six Manvantaras namely Swayabhuva, Swarachisha, Uttama, Tapasa, Ryvatha and Chakshusha have already passed off. At the end of Chakshusha Manvantara there was a king by name Sathyavratha. One day, when he was offering Tarpana after taking bath in the river Krithamala, he saw a fish in the water held by him in his hands. That fish was as minutely small as an atom. Within one or two days it grew gigantically and attained the proportions of one lakh yojanas. Thus the Lord in the guise of fish inculcated knowledge about his unique visage in the non plussed minds of the king and blessed the king with the position of Vyvasvatha Manu in his next birth and also bestowed him with salvation. This incarnation of Lord Sri Narayana is Matsyavathara. "Oh Lord! to be the minutest amongst the minutest and at the same time most gigantic amongst the biggest is the uniqueness of your visage which is ever blissful, which has not come from the soul and which is acclaimed by the Vedas. You have bestowed your special blessings on Vyvasvatha Manu by manifesting this feature of yours before him in your Matsyavathara (incarnation in the form of fish). Oh Lord Sri Moolamachandra!! I surrender myself at your Lotus feet". Sri Raghavendra has thus eulogised the Matsyavathara of Lord Sri Hari.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वेदसिद्धम् अणुतः अपि अणुभावम् मोददायि महतः अपि महत्त्वम् बिभ्रतम् प्रथयितुम् मनवे त्वाम् मीनताम् शरणम् यामि भवन्तम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मनवे वेदसिद्धम् अणुतः अपि अणुभावम् महतः अपि मोददायि महत्त्वम् प्रथयितुम् मीनताम् बिभ्रतं भवन्तं त्वां शरणं यामि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: I surrender unto You, who assumed the form of a fish (Matsyavatara) to demonstrate to Manu Your Vedic nature of being smaller than the smallest and greater than the greatest, bestowing immense bliss.

42.sa: वेदविप्लुतिकृतिं विधिजाड्यं हन्त हन्तुमदधाज्जलजन्म । मीनभावनभरेण ततो मे विस्तृणीहि विमलं प्रतिबोधम् ॥ ४२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "On another occasion at the end of the existence of the world, the giant Hayagreeva stole the Vedas emerging from the face of Brahma who was still sleeping. After waking up, Brahma who was puzzled as how to take up the task of creation of the world without the Vedas, was under a strange state of perplexity. Then you once again incarnated as Matsya and brought him out of his ignorance. Oh Lord of such prowess!! kindly bestow me with more and more knowledge". Sri Raghavendra has thus prayed the Lord.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वेदविप्लुतिकृतिम् विधिजाड्यम् हन्त हन्तुम् अदधात् जलजन्म मीनभावनभरेण ततः मे विस्तृणीहि विमलम् प्रतिबोधम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हन्त वेदविप्लुतिकृतिम् विधिजाड्यम् हन्तुम् मीनभावनभरेण जलजन्म अदधात् ततः मे विमलम् प्रतिबोधम् विस्तृणीहि
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet recalls how the Lord incarnated as a fish in the waters to dispel the stupor of Brahma caused by the loss of the Vedas, and prays to Him to expand pure, radiant wisdom in his mind.

43.sa: आत्मनैव कमठेन वितन्वन्मन्दरेण च भवानरणी द्वे । मथनतोत्थितहलाहलवह्निं होतुमिन्द्ररिपुवृन्दहवींषि ॥ ४३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Koormavathari! (incarnation in the form of turtle) when the devathas and the asuras were churning the ocean of milk with Mandaraparvatha as churning rod, that mountain started sinking in the ocean. You incarnated as Koorma to keep it afloat. Then you were like the lower Arani (the wood of the ficus religiosa used for kindling fire by attrition) and the Mandaraparvatha acted as the upper Arani. By the attrition of these two, you produced the fire of deadly poison to offer those asuras as havis (oblation) to that fire. Oh Lord of such wonderful feats!!! You are the one who bestows those men and women of devotion with prosperity and who destroys the asuras. I surrender myself at your lotus feet". Sri Raghavendra has thus offered his prayers to the Lord.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: आत्मना एव कमठेन वितन्वन् मन्दरेण च भवान् अरणी द्वे मथनतः उत्थित-हलाहल-वह्निं होतुम् इन्द्र-रिपु-वृन्द-हवींषि
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: भवान् आत्मना एव कमठेन च मन्दरेण द्वे अरणी वितन्वन् मथनतः उत्थित-हलाहल-वह्निं इन्द्र-रिपु-वृन्द-हवींषि होतुम् (इव प्रावर्तत)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Assuming the form of the divine Tortoise beneath Mount Mandara, the Lord acted like a pair of fire-sticks to generate the fiery Hālāhala poison from the churning of the ocean, as if to sacrifice the demons into it as oblations.

44.sa: आदिसूकरधरोद्धरणं ते सिन्धुबन्धुजठरात् श्रुतिगीतम् । मादृशां भवपयोधिगतानां रक्षणे परिचयं तदवैमः ॥ ४४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Ahi Varahamurthy (incarnation in the form of boar)! The Vedas and Puranas have acclaimed your stupendous feat of lifting Dharanidevi (the earth) from the ocean. It is my opinion that your feat is an act of rehearsal of uplift of people like me who are sunk deep in the ocean of the whirl and maze of mundane affairs". Sri Raghavendra has thus extolled the Lord Vishnu in the incarnation of Varaha.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: आदिसूकर धरोद्धरणम् ते सिन्धुबन्धुजठरात् श्रुतिगीतम् मादृशाम् भवपयोधिगतानाम् रक्षणे परिचयम् तत् अवैमः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे आदिसूकर सिन्धुबन्धुजठरात् ते श्रुतिगीतम् यत् धरोद्धरणम् तत् भवपयोधिगतानाम् मादृशाम् रक्षणे परिचयम् अवैमः
commentaries.gemini_summary: O Lord Varaha, your act of rescuing the Earth from the depths of the ocean, praised in the Vedas, is regarded by us as a rehearsal for saving souls like us who are drowning in the ocean of worldly existence.

45.sa: पूर्णचन्द्रगतलक्षणरेखा लक्षिता यदि तदैङ्ककलायाम् । संश्रितेन्दुमणिदंष्ट्रधरं स्यात्सोपमा भवति सूकररूप ॥ ४५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Varaharoopi Lord! if the lineament of stain which is in the middle of the moon, who is shining with sixteen parts, is separated and the stainless part of the moon is placed on it, it looks splendid. Likewise, at the time of you lifting Bhoodevi from the ocean, she, who is like the lineament of stain in the moon, shines brightly on your curved horn which appears like a stain on a new moon day.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्णचन्द्र-गत-लक्षण-रेखा लक्षिता यदि तदा अङ्क-कलायाम् संश्रित-इन्दुमणि-दंष्ट्र-धरम् स्यात् सा उपमा भवति सूकर-रूप
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे सूकर-रूप ! यदि पूर्णचन्द्र-गत-लक्षण-रेखा तदा अङ्क-कलायाम् लक्षिता [स्यात्, तर्हि] संश्रित-इन्दुमणि-दंष्ट्र-धरम् सा उपमा स्यात् भवति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Addressing Lord Varaha, the poet remarks that if the dark mark seen in a full moon were imagined to rest upon a single digit of the crescent moon, only that would serve as a fitting comparison to the dark Earth gracefully resting upon His shining tusk.

46.sa: तावकं नरहरेऽतिविरुद्धं वेषधारणमिदं तनुते नः । अत्यसंघाटितकर्म च कृत्वा पालये प्रणतमित्युपदेशम् ॥ ४६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Lakshminarasimha! it is popularly known that a protector always remains in a state of tranquility whereas a killer appears dreadfully frightening. But the reverse cannot be possible. Though you killed Hiranyakashipu, donning a dreadful form, you also protected Prahlada in the same form. Thus your killer form served as the protector too which is quite contradictory. Similarly the guise of a lion for a man and the guise of a man to a lion are also contradictory. You are both man as well as lion. Thus your form too looks strange. Therefore it is my opinion that by donning a form which is incomprehensible, you have proved that you can do things which others can't do in assuring those men and women of devotion that you always protect them by destroying their sins".
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तावकम् नरहरे अतिविरुद्धम् वेषधारणम् इदम् तनुते नः अत्यसंघाटित-कर्म च कृत्वा पालये प्रणतम् इति उपदेशम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे नरहरे इदम् तावकम् अतिविरुद्धम् वेषधारणम् अत्यसंघाटित-कर्म च कृत्वा प्रणतम् पालये इति उपदेशम् नः तनुते
commentaries.gemini_summary: O Lord Narasimha, this utterly paradoxical and contradictory form of Yours imparts the teaching to us that You will protect the surrendered devotee even by accomplishing seemingly impossible and contrary deeds.

47.sa: दारितोदरहिरण्यकशत्रोरान्त्रमाल्यकलितं तव रूपम् । नारसिंह कलयेऽननुभूतं शारदं जलधरं सहशम्पम् ॥ ४७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Narasimha! it is my opinion that you must have looked splendid like the cloud of an autumn, when you ripped open the stomach of Hiranyakashipu and wore his intestines as a garland around your neck which had no precedence".
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: दारित-उदर-हिरण्यक-शत्रोः आन्त्र-माल्य-कलितम् तव रूपम् नारसिंह कलये अननुभूतम् शारदम् जलधरम् सह-शम्पम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे नारसिंह ! दारित-उदर-हिरण्यक-शत्रोः तव आन्त्र-माल्य-कलितम् रूपम् अननुभूतम् सह-शम्पम् शारदम् जलधरम् कलये ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet addresses Lord Narasimha, reflecting that His unprecedented form—having ripped open the belly of the enemy Hiranyakashipu and wearing his entrails as a garland—resembles an autumnal cloud accompanied by streaks of lightning.

48.sa: जानतां निजमनः परमाणौ मातुमेव बलिनिग्रहदम्भात् । वामनं यदभवत्तव रूपं तत्सुखेन भगवन्हृदि कुर्मः ॥ ४८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord of infinite virtues! on the pretext of restraining the emperor Bali, you incarnated as Vamana. But your real intention was to enable the men of knowledge to firmly establish you in their minds which are as small as an atom. Otherwise how is it possible for them to concentrate their atom sized minds on your gigantic form of Trivikrama. Therefore, you donned the form of Vamana for the convenience of those men! I would strive to achieve a sense of fulfilment by meditating on this form of yours". Sri Raghavendra has thus extolled the incarnation of Vamana, who is not different from Lord Sri Moolaramachandra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: जानताम् निज-मनः-परमाणौ मातुम् एव बलि-निग्रह-दम्भात् वामनम् यत् अभवत् तव रूपम् तत् सुखेन भगवन् हृदि कुर्मः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: भगवन् जानताम् निज-मनः-परमाणौ मातुम् एव बलि-निग्रह-दम्भात् तव यत् वामनम् रूपम् अभवत् तत् सुखेन हृदि कुर्मः
commentaries.gemini_summary: O Lord, under the guise of subduing King Bali, You assumed the tiny form of Vamana so that the wise could measure and fit You within their subtle, atom-like minds; we joyfully enshrine that very form in our hearts.

49.sa: चन्द्रमा इव भुवो रचयन्नक्षत्रयोगमपि यस्त्वमलासीः । तेन शात्रवयशोम्बुजराजीमुद्रणं तव कृतिं बहु मन्ये ॥ ४९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Hari! the moon sparkles brightly by causing relationship between the stars and earth. Likewise, you looked splendid by depriving all the Kshatriyas of their relationship with this world incarnating as Parashurama of such prowess. You caused the flowers of fame and reputation of your enemies (Kshatriyas) to shrink and transformed the group of those lotus flowers into buds. I salute and worship your marvellous feat.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चन्द्रमाः इव भुवः रचयन् न-क्षत्र-योगम् अपि यः त्वम् अलासीः तेन शात्रव-यशः-अम्बुज-राजी-मुद्रणम् तव कृतिम् बहु मन्ये
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: चन्द्रमाः इव भुवः नक्षत्रयोगम् (न-क्षत्र-योगम्) अपि रचयन् यः त्वम् अलासीः तेन शात्रव-यशः-अम्बुज-राजी-मुद्रणं तव कृतिं बहु मन्ये ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet praises the Lord (as Parashurama) who shone while rendering the earth devoid of Kshatriyas, just as the moon shines associated with the stars, and extols His wonderful feat of closing the blossoming lotuses of His enemies' fame.

50.sa: तारणे दुरितनीरनिधेर्नः सेतुभावमचिरेण यियासोः । भासते तव विभो करुणायाः पूर्वरङ्ग इव दक्षिणसेतुः ॥ ५0 ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Moolarama! your kindness facilitates us to cross the ocean of our sins like a bridge. The bridge you built across the southern sea stands looking splendid as a prelude in this context".
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तारणे दुरितनीरनिधेः नः सेतुभावम् अचिरेण यियासोः भासते तव विभो करुणायाः पूर्वरङ्गः इव दक्षिणसेतुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: विभो दुरितनीरनिधेः तारणे अचिरेण नः सेतुभावम् यियासोः तव करुणायाः दक्षिणसेतुः पूर्वरङ्गः इव भासते
commentaries.gemini_summary: O Lord, the southern bridge built by You across the sea appears like a mere prelude to Your compassion, which swiftly acts as a bridge helping us cross the vast ocean of our sins.

51.sa: बन्धनाय कृतमात्मजनन्या तादृशं च गुणमङ्गचकरोर्यत् । तेन निर्गुणमतानि निरस्यन्दर्शयस्यपि निजां गुणवत्ताम् ॥ ५१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Krishna! your mother Yashoda bound you with an ordinary rope used for tying cows and calves and you too accepted it. Thus you exhibited before the men and women of devotion that you were an embodiment of infinite qualities dispelling the philosophy which advocated that the Brahman was devoid of any physical form and also qualities.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: बन्धनाय कृतम् आत्मजनन्या तादृशम् च गुणम् अङ्ग चकरोः यत् तेन निर्गुणमतानि निरस्यन् दर्शयसि अपि निजाम् गुणवत्ताम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अङ्ग आत्मजनन्या बन्धनाय कृतं तादृशं गुणं च यत् अकरोः तेन निर्गुणमतानि निरस्यन् निजां गुणवत्ताम् अपि दर्शयसि
commentaries.gemini_summary: O Lord, by submitting to the binding rope (guna) tied by Your own mother, You refuted the philosophies advocating a quality-less (nirguna) Brahman and revealed Your own possession of auspicious divine qualities (gunavattva).

52.sa: सर्वदेवरथचेष्टनमङ्गीकुर्वतस्तव सदैव जगत्याम् । अर्जुनैकरथसारथिभावो विस्मयाय विदुषां न कथंचित् ॥ ५२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord! Your act of accepting the task of driving Arjuna's chariot does not surprise the men of knowledge, because it is you who controls the actions of the bodies of all living beings". Explanation: The Shrutis proclaim that the bodies of all the living beings are the chariots of Lord Sri Hari. Oh Lord! as the bodies of living beings are your chariots, you have taken up the responsibility of driving those chariots. Therefore it is not surprising that you drove the chariot of Arjuna. As per the quote, Lord Sri Krishna acts as the charioteer of the chariots (bodies) of all the virtuous living beings as well as the chariot of Arjuna. The Lord of such prowess is divinely great.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सर्वदेवरथचेष्टनम् अङ्गीकुर्वतः तव सदा एव जगत्याम् अर्जुन-एक-रथ-सारथि-भावः विस्मयाय विदुषाम् न कथञ्चित्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: जगत्याम् सदा एव सर्वदेवरथचेष्टनम् अङ्गीकुर्वतः तव अर्जुनैकरथसारथिभावः विदुषां कथञ्चित् विस्मयाय न (भवति)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Since the Lord is perpetually responsible for directing the chariot-like bodies of all beings in the universe, the wise are not in the least surprised by His assuming the role of charioteer for Arjuna's single chariot.

53.sa: त्वं कुचेलमुनिमीश कुचेलाद्यर्पणेन कृतवान्कुचेलम् । सोभवत्तदपि चारुकुचेलालंकृतस्तदिदमद्भुतमासीत् ॥ ५३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Krishna! when the saintly Kuchela offered you beaten rice packed in torn out cloth, you blessed him by gifting new silk clothes (Peethambara). Therefore it is really surprising that Kuchela who was not attached to earthly life continued to wear torn out clothes in spite of you blessing him with new clothes.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: त्वम् कुचेल-मुनिम् ईश कुचेल-आदि-अर्पणेन कृतवान् कुचेलम् सः अभवत् तत् अपि चारु-कुचेल-अलङ्कृतः तत् इदम् अद्भुतम् आसीत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे ईश ! त्वम् कुचेल-आदि-अर्पणेन कुचेल-मुनिम् कुचेलम् कृतवान्, तत् अपि सः चारु-कुचेल-अलङ्कृतः अभवत्, तत् इदम् अद्भुतम् आसीत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: O Lord, when the sage Kuchela offered You modest beaten rice tied in torn rags, You showered him with riches and fine garments; yet, despite being adorned in such splendour, he still remained Kuchela, which was truly a wondrous marvel.

54.sa: एवमादिविविधैरवतारैः पालिताखिलजनौघ ममाघम् । सन्निरस्य कमलास्य नमस्यां स्वीकुरुष्व रघुवंशवतंस ॥ ५४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Oh Lord Sri Moolarama! You are blessing all those virtuous men and women by incarnating as Matsya, Koorma, and other such forms. You are the greatest in the lineage of Raghu! the lotus appears pale in comparison with your beautiful face!! Oh Lord!! kindly destroy all my sins and accept my obeisance.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: एवम्-आदि-विविधैः अवतारैः पालित-अखिल-जन-ओघ मम अघम् सन्निरस्य कमल-आस्य नमस्याम् स्वीकुरुष्व रघु-वंश-अवतंस
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे एवमादिविविधैः अवतारैः पालिताखिलजनौघ हे कमलास्य हे रघुवंशवतंस मम अघम् सन्निरस्य नमस्याम् स्वीकुरुष्व
commentaries.gemini_summary: Addressing Lord Rama—who protects all people through various incarnations, possesses a lotus-like countenance, and adorns the Raghu dynasty—the devotee prays for the complete destruction of his sins and the acceptance of his humble obeisance.

55.sa: इत्युदीर्य विनतोपि नयेन प्रार्थितस्तदनु संसदमागात् । सत्पथं विशदयन् समुदीतः पूर्वशैलमिव कैरवबन्धुः ॥ ५५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thus extolling Lord Sri Narayana, Sri Raghavendra paid his obeisance to the Lord. Then he went to the conference hall as requested by his attendants. The moon rises above Udayaparvatha spreading his light all over the sky on which the devatas and stars tread. The water lilies get elated and bloom when the moon rises. Likewise Sri Raghavendra reached Udayashyla (Conference Hall) spreading the light of knowledge all over the path of the virtuous and delighting the flowers of water lily (noble men of knowledge, on his way).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: इति उदीर्य विनतः अपि नयेन प्रार्थितः तत् अनु संसदम् आगात् सत्पथम् विशदयन् समुदीतः पूर्वशैलम् इव कैरवबन्धुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: इति उदीर्य विनतः अपि नयेन प्रार्थितः तदनु सत्पथम् विशदयन् समुदीतः कैरवबन्धुः पूर्वशैलम् इव संसदम् आगात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having spoken thus and bowed respectfully, Sri Raghavendra, upon being requested with humility, proceeded to the assembly hall, illuminating the path of virtue just as the newly risen moon ascends the eastern mountain, lighting up the sky.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The conference hall which Sri Raghavendra entered was heavenly and divinely affluent. It was provided with ventilators at the top of its walls. Those ventilators which were studded with fabulous gems were made of moon stones. When the flood waters of the celestial Ganges rushed towards the earth through those ventilators the force of the flood waters pushed the milky white swans towards the earth. Being unable to return, those swans are now limping and wallowing as white umbrellas and chamaras of Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रांशु यत् मणि-गवाक्ष-विनिर्यत्-द्योसरित्-जल-वशात् समुपेत्य अङ्गमाः इव लुठन्ति यतीन्दु-च्छत्र-चामर-मिषेण मरालाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: प्रांशु यत्-मणि-गवाक्ष-विनिर्यत्-द्योसरित्-जल-वशात् समुपेत्य मरालाः अङ्गमाः इव यतीन्दु-च्छत्र-चामर-मिषेण लुठन्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Swans, swept down by the waters of the celestial river flowing through the lofty jeweled windows of the grand hall and unable to move, appear to roll about in the guise of the white umbrellas and fly-whisks serving Sri Raghavendra.

57.sa: व्योमलङ्घनगदेन समुद्यन् यन्निरुद्धगतयो दिवि ताराः । तत्प्रभुं शरणयन्ति यतीन्दुं मौक्तिकासनगमौक्तिकदम्भात् ॥ ५७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The stars in the sky above the earth intended to move still upwards and enter the heaven. But some saints who were moving still more upwards prevented those stars from moving upwards and advised them not to compete with them. Then those stars decided to pray Sri Raghavendra, the king of saints to advise those saints to desist from becoming hurdles in their path. The poet has exaggerated that those stars appeared to have surrendered at the lotus feet of Sri Raghavendra on the pretext of serving him as the pearls of his throne.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्योम-लङ्घन-गदेन समुद्यत्-यति-निरुद्ध-गतयः दिवि ताराः तत्-प्रभुम् शरणयन्ति यति-इन्दुम् मौक्तिक-आसन-ग-मौक्तिक-दम्भात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: व्योम-लङ्घन-गदेन समुद्यत्-यति-निरुद्ध-गतयः दिवि ताराः मौक्तिक-आसन-ग-मौक्तिक-दम्भात् तत्-प्रभुम् यतीन्दुम् शरणयन्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Obstructed in their skyward ascent by other rising ascetics, the stars in the heavens appear to seek refuge with their master, Sri Raghavendra (the moon among ascetics), under the guise of pearls adorning his pearl-studded seat.

58.sa: नाहुतं श्रितवतां सततं यस्तम्भदुर्गणलयो भवितेति । संनियच्छति निगृह्य समस्तं स्तम्भमप्यतिमहान्तमसौ यत् ॥ ५८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra with his divine power cures all the physical and mental maladies such as laziness, ignorance, however serious they may be. When that is the case, it is not surprising that he destroys all the hurdles in the path of those men and women who surrender before him. The great saint and the king of saints Sri Raghavendra destroys all kinds of impediments. Therefore it is not necessary to say that the great saint destroys all the hurdles in the path of those stars as quoted in the previous stanza.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: न अद्भुतम् श्रितवताम् सततम् यत् स्तम्भ-दुर्गण-लयः भविता इति संनियच्छति निगृह्य समस्तम् स्तम्भम् अपि अति-महान्तम् असौ यत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: असौ समस्तम् अतिमहान्तम् अपि स्तम्भम् निगृह्य संनियच्छति यत्, श्रितवताम् सततम् स्तम्भ-दुर्गण-लयः भविता इति न अद्भुतम् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Since he completely restrains and destroys even the most massive pillar (or deepest stupor), it is no wonder that those who take refuge in him constantly see the dissolution of all afflictions and bad qualities such as inertia and dullness.

59.sa: संचरन् क्वचन यत्र दिदृक्षुश्चन्द्रकान्तमणिमण्टपतौघः । आहतः शशिरुचा बत सिद्धः पर्यहास्यत परन्नगतेन ॥ ५९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Once two demigods descended on the earth to have a glimpse of Sri Raghavendra. They came near the mantap made of moonstone where the great saint was shining splendidly. One of them came below the mantap to have a close look and the other one stayed at the top of the mantap. Both who were shining brilliantly in the lustre of the moon stone, looked like Moon. The demi god at the top thought that it was only he who was shining, because he was unaware of the fact that the bottom of the mantap too was made of moon stone. He ridiculed the one at the bottom of the mantap thinking that the latter has missed the opportunity of shining like him. Thus he cut a sorry figure with his ignorance. The great saint Sri Raghavendra was seated in the mantap of such marvel made of moon stone. This is the summary of this stanza.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: संचरन् क्वचन यत्र दिदृक्षुः चन्द्रकान्त-मणि-मण्टप-तौघः आहतः शशिरुचा बत सिद्धः पर्यहास्यत परन्नगतेन
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यत्र क्वचन संचरन् दिदृक्षुः चन्द्रकान्तमणिमण्टपतौघः शशिरुचा आहतः सिद्धः बत परन्नगतेन पर्यहास्यत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Desiring to catch a glimpse of the great saint Raghavendra in the moonstone pavilion, a visiting Siddha at the base was illuminated by its moon-like brilliance and was unknowingly ridiculed by another Siddha stationed at the top.

60.sa: संचरन् शिखिमुखोरगपीतस्वाश्वयानिललयातत्सघनेषु । सम्पतत्सु पतितो भुवि सिद्धा विस्मयं दधति हन्त यदन्तः॥ ६० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Some peacocks which were holding snakes, their food, in their beaks were flying near the spheres of clouds in the sky above the moon stone mantap in which Sri Raghavendra was sitting. Those snakes were swallowing the wind which was holding the clouds, even when they were at the threshold of death. Those clouds which were devoid of wind started showering rains on the earth. Some demi gods who were moving about in the sky during that time too fell on the earth along with showers. When those demi gods beheld the beauty of that moon stone mantap in which the great saint was sitting, they were astonished at its unprecedented marvel and started showering praises on it.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: संचरत्-शिखि-मुख-उरग-पीत-स्वाश्रय-अनिल-लयात् तत्-स-घनेषु सम्पतत्सु भुवि पतिताः सिद्धाः हन्त यत्-अन्तः विस्मयं दधति
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: संचरत्-शिखि-मुख-उरग-पीत-स्वाश्रय-अनिल-लयात् तत्-स-घनेषु सम्पतत्सु भुवि पतिताः सिद्धाः हन्त यद्-अन्तः विस्मयं दधति।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When snakes held in the beaks of moving peacocks swallowed the atmospheric winds supporting the clouds, the clouds along with the celestial Siddhas fell to the ground; there, inside the marvelous pavilion of the Guru, the fallen Siddhas were filled with wonder.

61.sa: न त्यजन्ति मिहिरं तव यात्राङ्गारचर्वणचणा हि चकोराः । पक्षिभाषणकृते यदि नामावालिखिल्यनिगमाध्ययनानि ॥ ६१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: There are two types of Greek partridge, those who survive on fire and those who survive on moonbeam. The birds which swallow fire never separate from the sun and they sparkle in moon light. Therefore the birds in sleep too begin to twitter under the illusion that the sun has already risen. Before the sun rises, sixty thousand thumb sized Valakhilyas praise the sun chanting many quotes from the Vedas. Since the moon is shining like sun now, I consider the twittering of those birds as the quotes of the Vedas chanted by Valakhilyas.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: न त्यजन्ति मिहिरम् तव यात्रा-अङ्गार-चर्वण-चणाः हि चकोराः पक्षि-भाषण-कृते यदि नाम आ-वालखिल्य-निगम-अध्ययनानि
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तव यात्रा-अङ्गार-चर्वण-चणाः चकोराः मिहिरं न त्यजन्ति हि यदि नाम पक्षि-भाषण-कृते आ-वालखिल्य-निगम-अध्ययनानि (स्युः)
commentaries.gemini_summary: The cakora birds, fond of eating the sparks generated during your march, do not leave the radiant sun; their chirping resembles the continuous Vedic recitations chanted by the Vālakhilya sages.

62.sa: तत्र चन्द्रमणिकुट्टिमसिन्धौ मौक्तिकासनमये भुजगेन्द्रे । राजते रघुपुरन्दरनामा पाटलाम्बरधरः परमात्मा ॥ ६२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The place where that ineffable moon-stone mantap was situated looked splendid like the ocean of milk. Sri Raghavendra, the great saint wearing ochre coloured clothes seated on the throne of pearls there coruscated like Lord Sri Narayana reclining on Sesha in the ocean of milk. Those who have profound devotion in the God coruscate like God with his special blessings. This is known as the state of assimilation to the deity in salvation. Therefore this comparative description by the poet is in conformity with the established truth. Sri Raghavendra wears ochre coloured clothes, whereas Lord Sri Hari wears yellow coloured silk clothes. The dissimilitude between them is indicated by the quote here. The words also indicate this dissimilarity, meaning Sri Raghavendra always meditates through his heart and mind on Lord Sri Narayana, the supreme, and on Sri Lakshmidevi, the supreme amongst those who are not independent.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तत्र चन्द्रमणिकुट्टिमसिन्धौ मौक्तिकासनमये भुजगेन्द्रे राजते रघुपुरन्दरनामा पाटलाम्बरधरः परमात्मा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तत्र चन्द्रमणिकुट्टिमसिन्धौ मौक्तिकासनमये भुजगेन्द्रे पाटलाम्बरधरः रघुपुरन्दरनामा परमात्मा राजते ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: In that ocean-like floor paved with moonstones, seated upon a throne of pearls resembling the serpent king Shesha, Sri Raghavendra (Raghupurandara), adorned in ochre robes, shone resplendently like the Supreme Lord.

63.sa: केचन प्रतिपुरन्दरमेनं पर्युपासत बुधाः प्रतिमान्तैः । कुर्वतेत्र पदपूर्वसमस्यापूरणं च कवयः पुरतोस्य ॥ ६३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Some men of knowledge offered their services to Sri Raghavendra who was like or equal to Devendra in the form of discussions on those literary works which depict the true meanings of the Vedas like Upanishads and Bramhasootras. The poet amongst them solved puzzles in the presence of the great saint in the assembly of scholars. Explanation: The Devathas in different guises came to the assembly of scholars and offered their services to Sri Raghavendra, the great Saint in the form of discussions on Upanishads and Brahmasootras which depict the true meanings of the Vedas.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: केचन प्रतिपुरन्दरम् एनम् पर्युपासत बुधाः प्रतिमान्तैः कुर्वते अत्र पदपूर्वसमस्यापूरणम् च कवयः पुरतः अस्य
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: केचन बुधाः प्रतिमान्तैः प्रतिपुरन्दरम् एनम् पर्युपासत च अत्र कवयः अस्य पुरतः पदपूर्वसमस्यापूरणं कुर्वते ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Some scholars attended upon Sri Raghavendra, who resembled Indra, with profound philosophical discourses, while poets performed spontaneous poetic completions and solved metrical riddles in his presence.

64.sa: श्रियः पतिः श्रीमति शासितुं जगन्निपीय यस्य क्षितिरक्षिणः कलाः । श्रियः कुरूणामधिपस्य पालनीः श्रियः स दत्तान्विह ते पुरःस्थितः ॥ ६४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Lord Sri Narayana incarnated as Sri Krishna in order to protect this world and to engage the souls of infinite numbers in their duties. When Duryodhana was behaving insolently after deceivably usurping all the wealth of the Pandavas, Sri Krishna got him killed by Bheemasena and returned their wealth to the Pandavas. Thus the Lord Sri Hari with his "Poornamsha" has incarnated as Matsya, Koorma, Rama, Krishna and other forms on this earth. He also protects this world with his "aveshas" in Balarama, Prithu, Sanatkumara and others. The Lord of such prowess in His infinite incarnations is present in the idol of Sri Moolarama accompanied by his consort Sri Seethadevi, the nithyaviyogini (always would be with her consort) who is not different from Sri Laxmidevi. Sri Chaturmukha Brahma himself has worshipped this idol known as "Chaturyuga moorthi" which is the presiding deity of the Mutt, the throne of knowledge of which is adorned by none other than that great saint auspiciously named as Sri Raghavendratheertha. "Let this Lord Moolarama being pleased with your worship, prayer and meditation bestow prosperity and success related to both worlds on those who have profound devotion in guru, Pranadeva and Lord Sri Hari". Thus praying, the poet Sri Narayanacharya has concluded this great epic.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रियः पतिः श्रीमति शासितुम् जगत् निपीय यस्य क्षिति-रक्षिणः कलाः श्रियः कुरूणाम् अधिपस्य पालनीः श्रियः सः दत्तात् नु इह ते पुरःस्थितः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीमति जगत् शासितुम् यस्य क्षितिरक्षिणः कलाः निपीय कुरूणाम् अधिपस्य पालनीः श्रियः (अभवन्) सः पुरःस्थितः श्रियः पतिः इह ते श्रियः दत्तात् नु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: May the supreme Lord of Sri (Moolarama), who manifests His portions to protect and govern the world and sustain the fortunes of the virtuous rulers, and who is presently enshrined before you, graciously grant you all divine prosperity and auspiciousness.

65.sa: सन्तं श्रीरमणं प्रियं यतिवरं व्यासस्य भावे भृशं दुर्वारामितमायिभिक्षुतिमिरे पर्वस्थचन्द्रं भुवि । सत्संघस्तुतमिष्टदक्षितिरुहं वन्दारुविप्राश्रयं तं नत्वा सकलो दुरूहसुदृशं संयाति विद्यादिकम् ॥ ६५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra is dearest to Lord Sri Narayana, the consort of Sri Lakshmi. He is always engaged in writing books and teaching the meanings of the Geetha, Upanishads and Brahmasootras in conformity with the views of Lord Sri Vedavyasa. He is the greatest among all the saints on earth. He is like the moon of a full moon day in destroying the darkness caused by the views of those who advocate Mayavada. He is like Kalpavruksha, for those who adore him. He bestows prosperity and success on those virtuous brahmins who constantly prostrate at his lotus feet. Those who prostrate before him and those who eulogise him constantly, acquire spiritual knowledge which is beyond one's imagination and which cannot be described in words. Profound knowledge, opulence, expertise in music and sculpture, begetting children and other such wishes of those who worship Sri Raghavendra with profound devotion are sure to be fulfilled.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सन्तम् श्रीरमणप्रियम् यतिवरम् व्यासस्य भावे भृशम् दुर्वार-अमित-मायि-भिक्षु-तिमिरे पर्वस्थ-चन्द्रम् भुवि सत्-सङ्घ-स्तुतम् इष्टद-क्षितिरुहम् वन्दारु-विप्र-आश्रयम् तम् नत्वा सकलः दुरूह-सुदृशम् संयाति विद्या-आदिकम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: भुवि सन्तम् श्रीरमणप्रियम् यतिवरम् व्यासस्य भावे भृशम् दुर्वारामितमायिभिक्षुतिमिरे पर्वस्थचन्द्रम् सत्सङ्घस्तुतम् इष्टदक्षितिरुहम् वन्दारुविप्राश्रयम् तम् नत्वा सकलः दुरूहसुदृशम् विद्यादिकम् संयाति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: By bowing to Guru Raghavendra—the foremost ascetic beloved of Lord Vishnu, devoted to Vyasa's intent, a full moon dispelling the darkness of Mayavada, a wish-fulfilling tree, and the refuge of pious scholars—everyone attains profound knowledge and all desirable blessings.

66.sa: श्रीमत्कश्यपवंशवार्धिशशिनः षड्दर्शनीवल्लभ- श्रीलक्ष्मीनरसिंहवित्तविदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ । जातेनार्यदयासुधामयगिरा नारायणेनोदिते काव्ये चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये सर्गोन्तिमोभूदिह ॥ ६६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thus concludes the tenth and final canto of the epic "Sri Raghavendra Vijaya" enchanting with nectareous words composed by Narayanacharya with the blessings of his father. Narayanacharya who had his education from his father was the son of the couple Venkatamba and Lakshminarasimhacharya who was an erudite scholar in all the six shastras and who was born and shone like a moon in the ocean of Kashyapagothra named after that virtuous and scholarly sage Kashyapa. English translation of the tenth and final canto of the epic "Sri Raghavendra Vijaya" composed by Sri Narayanacharya concluded.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्री-वेङ्कटाम्बा-मणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधा-मय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते चारुणि राघवेन्द्र-विजये काव्ये इह अन्तिमः सर्गः अभूत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीमत्कश्यपवंशवार्धिशशिनः षड्दर्शनीवल्लभश्रीलक्ष्मीनरसिंहवित्तविदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ जातेन आर्यदयासुधामयगिरा नारायणेन उदिते चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये काव्ये इह अन्तिमः सर्गः अभूत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: This verse concludes the epic Raghavendra Vijaya, composed with speech enriched by the nectar of his preceptor's grace by Narayanacharya, the son of the jewel-like Venkatamba and Lakshminarasimhacharya, who was a master of the six philosophical systems and the moon of the glorious Kashyapa lineage.
